correctness.rationale: The repaired theorem uses dimensionless time and explicitly fixes the units issue: r_*~Omega^2/(2J) does not imply r_*->0 along arbitrary j->infinity (e.g. Omega=j,J=j^2); with Omega fixed it does. CHSH is taken over nondegenerate projective spin observables. In the occupied subspace, A has energy -j and (B,S) is the block with diagonals -j,j and off-diagonals 1. Expanding B in its two eigenvectors cancels the entire lower-mode error; the remaining upper-mode vector is sin(theta)(exp(-i omega t)-exp(i omega t))/sqrt(2) times its unit eigenvector. Its norm bound yields the stated projector trace-norm bound pointwise and after averaging against any age law. Integration against qe^{-qt} gives the effective 00/11 block; the correlation singular values are 1,|kappa/(1+kappa^2)|,|kappa/(1+kappa^2)|. The Tsirelson operator-norm bound gives the Lipschitz constant 2 sqrt(2). The profile tends to 2 at both ends, so a positive profile gap off a compact neighborhood plus the all-rate bound gives interior attainment by continuity and forces every optimizer to kappa=1 asymptotically (no finite-j uniqueness claimed). The dropped fixed-j statement is correct under the same nondegenerate convention: dephasing leaves T_{yy}=1/[2(1+j^2)] and T_{zz}=(2j^2+1)/[2(1+j^2)]. An independent column-stacked stationary solve in /tmp/opencode/frozen_1_2_3_checks.py confirmed finite examples, e.g. j=40 at q=delta gives 2.235637382686. Read the uploaded check.py but did not execute it.

value.rationale: An explicit time-uniform two-state approximation keeps the correct slow energy gap, avoiding secular phase errors and allowing arbitrarily long or widely distributed ages. Its all-rate consequence rules out better Bell values at escaping reset scales and answers an optimization question not settled by a scaling-family peak. The selected physical scale and its dimensional qualification are usable without claiming newness for the old window or endpoints.
